physics_conclusion: Rotating (Kerr) black holes undergo a polymer/spectral-action bounce mirroring the Schwarzschild case. BKL rotational decoupling guarantees that near the would-be singularity (α→-∞ in Misner coordinates) the angular-momentum potential is exponentially suppressed relative to the Kasner centrifugal walls (V_rot/V_curv < 10^{-10} at α=-10), reducing near-neck dynamics to an AVTD Kasner bounce with rotation as a conserved charge. A finite bounce neck exists for all sub-extremal Kerr (a < M); angular momentum J is strictly conserved (axial Killing vector survives quantum corrections); NEC violation is confined to a Planckian ~3.5/μ window (same as spherical); and Hawking temperature correctly goes to zero at extremality (third law of black hole mechanics), eliminating naked singularities in the over-extremal regime (a > M has no trapped neck because over-extremal Kerr is not formed from physical collapse).
